definitions.explanation: The third-born son in a family.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三男|さんなん}だ。
うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{三男|さんなん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦{小学校|しょうがっこう}→小学校：01055_shougakkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: Our third son will start elementary school next year.

examples.japanese: {三男|さんなん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{自由|じゆう}→自由：01148_jiyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{育|そだ}てられる→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It's said that third sons are often raised with more freedom.

notes:
BIRTH ORDER TERMS (sons):
- ⟦{長男|ちょうなん}→長男：14519_chounan⟧: eldest son
- ⟦{次男|じなん}→次男：13210_jinan⟧: second son
- {三男|さんなん}: third son
- {四男|よんなん}: fourth son

BIRTH ORDER TERMS (daughters):
- ⟦{長女|ちょうじょ}→長女：14518_choujo⟧: eldest daughter
- ⟦{次女|じじょ}→次女：15831_jijo⟧: second daughter
- ⟦{三女|さんじょ}→三女：10690_sanjo⟧: third daughter

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese families, the ⟦{長男|ちょうなん}→長男：14519_chounan⟧ was expected to inherit the family house and business. Younger sons had more freedom to pursue their own paths, which sometimes led to the stereotype that {三男|さんなん} are more easygoing.
